name: TWO WORLDS, ONE FRAME
message:
Take a picture and transform it into a seamless split-frame digital collage in the tradition of contemporary contrast-collage artists who juxtapose two starkly different realities within a single continuous photograph. The subject occupies one half of the frame, fully integrated into an IDYLLIC WORLD scene. The other half of the SAME continuous frame — sharing consistent lighting logic, horizon lines, and perspective so it reads as one impossible photograph, not two pasted together — depicts THE OTHER SIDE OF THE WORLD, a starkly harder reality. The two halves meet at a deliberate visual SEAM that makes the collision unmistakable rather than hidden.

CRITICAL:
• The seam must be a clear formal device (see SEAM options) — this is a collage confronting the viewer with contrast, not a seamless blend that hides the split
• Color grading should shift meaningfully across the seam — warmer/more saturated on the idyllic side, cooler/more desaturated on the other
• The subject should appear ONLY on the idyllic side, fully present and photorealistic; the other side should read as environment and circumstance, not as a depiction of the subject or any other identifiable person in distress
• This format is meant to provoke reflection on inequality and contrast, not to shock or sensationalize

options.text: Relaxing on a sun-drenched beach vacation
A plush, softly-lit living room at home
A birthday celebration with balloons and cake
A sunny park picnic with friends
A cozy reading nook by a fireplace
A summer pool party
A holiday feast at an abundant dinner table
A spa day, calm and unhurried
Cheering in a bright, joyful concert crowd
A graduation ceremony, proud and triumphant

options.groupName: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE WORLD

options.text: A quiet tent encampment at dusk, no people in distress
A drought-cracked, barren field stretching to the horizon
A flood-submerged street, water reflecting a gray sky
A neighborhood hazed by distant wildfire smoke
An empty, weathered building facade showing age and hardship
A line of empty folding chairs at a dawn food-bank distribution
A makeshift shelter built under a highway overpass
A polluted river choked with visible waste
A dense, overcrowded informal settlement rooftop view
A single bare lightbulb in an unfinished concrete room
A jagged, torn-paper edge between the two halves
A hard, deliberate vertical split with no blending
A diagonal fold line, like a photograph creased in half
A mirrored reflection seam, as if across still water
A gradual fading gradient dissolve between the two realities
A cracked-glass fracture line running through the frame
A gradual desaturation gradient from vivid color to gray
A film-strip sprocket-hole divide, like two frames of film
A visibly stitched-together seam with coarse thread
A stark boundary from bright light into deep shadow

additionalInstructions: HARD CONSTRAINTS: Do not depict graphic violence, injury, death, or bodies of any kind. Do not depict any real, specific, named current or historical conflict, disaster, or country/region intended to be recognized as a real event. Do not depict any real, identifiable public figure. Do not depict the subject, or any other person, appearing distressed, injured, or in danger on the 'other side' — that side should be told through environment and circumstance, never through a person's suffering. The goal is to provoke reflection on inequality and contrast, evoking empathy through juxtaposition rather than shock through explicit suffering.
